articles.title: ISTQB CTFL in 2027: is it still worth it? What changes, what does not
articles.excerpt: Short answer: yes if you are starting in testing or switching into it, with realistic expectations. CTFL v4.0 is still the current syllabus and ISTQB has announced no new Foundation version at the dat…
articles.body: Short answer: yes if you are starting in testing or switching into it, with realistic expectations. CTFL v4.0 is still the current syllabus and ISTQB has announced no new Foundation version at the date of writing (19 November 2026). What changes in 2027 The CTFL syllabus itself: nothing announced. The current version is v4.0 (released 9 May 2023, downloadable as v4.0.1 on istqb.org). The ISTQB CTFL page announces no new version and no sunset date. Holders of older versions stay certified, no re-take is mandated. Exam format today: 40 questions, 26 points to pass, 60 minutes (+25% for non-native language). What does change in 2027 around CTFL: CTFL-AT (Agile Tester): exams and training end on 6 May 2027 (English) and 6 November 2027 (other languages). Agile content is already in CTFL v4.0.

articles.title: Interviews changed with AI, so I built a practice tool for the new skills
articles.excerpt: AI writes a lot of code now. What's left for us, and what interviews increasingly test, is working with code we didn't write. That's three skills: Debugging someone else's code from a bug report. Addi…
articles.body: AI writes a lot of code now. What's left for us, and what interviews increasingly test, is working with code we didn't write. That's three skills: Debugging someone else's code from a bug report. Adding a feature without breaking what already works. Reviewing a pull request and deciding whether it can merge. Most practice sites still ask you to write an algorithm from scratch. So I built DevDrill , an open-source app that runs on your own machine. How it works You get a small, realistic project in a VS Code-style editor in your browser, in JavaScript or TypeScript. Debug: a bug report, a few files and failing tests. Find the cause and fix it. When you submit, hidden tests check the edge cases, so patching only the symptom usually fails.

articles.title: Audio to MIDI Explained: Why One Voice Is Easy and a Full Song Is Hard (With a Python Example)
articles.excerpt: By Tania Alwan "Audio to MIDI" sounds like a single feature: drop in a recording, get notes out. Under the hood it is two very different problems. Turning one sung or played melody into MIDI is a solv…
articles.body: By Tania Alwan "Audio to MIDI" sounds like a single feature: drop in a recording, get notes out. Under the hood it is two very different problems. Turning one sung or played melody into MIDI is a solved-enough task you can script in about 30 lines of Python. Turning a full mix with chords, bass and drums into clean MIDI is still an active research area. This post explains why, and shows a working monophonic converter. What MIDI actually stores A MIDI file does not contain sound. It contains events: Note on / note off with a pitch number (0 to 127) and a velocity Timing , in ticks relative to a tempo Optional controller data (pitch bend, sustain pedal, and so on) So audio to MIDI means answering three questions for every note: which pitch , when does it start , and when does it end .

articles.title: Why Photoshot keeps the original color when you edit in black and white
articles.excerpt: Photoshot Looks development journal, part 1 of 9. In the first build of Silver for Photoshot Looks, I converted a three-color test image to black and white and tried two different Color Filter hues. B…
articles.body: Photoshot Looks development journal, part 1 of 9. In the first build of Silver for Photoshot Looks, I converted a three-color test image to black and white and tried two different Color Filter hues. Both produced identical pixels. I could see the same problem with a Control Point. Changing how strongly it selected by color had no effect after the image went monochrome. Nik Silver Efex gave me a clue. It opens in neutral black and white, yet it still lets you brighten or darken parts of the image based on their original hues. Its local controls also let you adjust lightness and chroma selectivity separately. Those behaviors suggested a design for Photoshot. Keep the original color available for selection, and apply the edit to the image as it looks now.

A single-page app that builds its content in the browser can look nearly empty to them.

articles.title: A Green Signup Test Can Verify The Wrong Account
articles.excerpt: Test A submits a signup form using qa@example.com. Its verification email is delayed, and the test times out. Test B starts with the same address, submits the same form, and waits for an email whose s…
articles.body: Test A submits a signup form using qa@example.com . Its verification email is delayed, and the test times out. Test B starts with the same address, submits the same form, and waits for an email whose subject contains “Verify.” A's message arrives first. B reads it, follows the link, sees a success page, and goes green. Every individual assertion can pass while B's signup is broken. The failure is a correlation problem. Email delivery is asynchronous, and a shared mailbox has no idea which Playwright worker triggered a message. A subject filter narrows the search. It does not identify the transaction. Disclosure: I build InboxRhino , a receive-only test inbox API. The test design below works with any mailbox that your CI job can read.

articles.title: My Rank Check Was Accurate. For the Wrong Country.
articles.excerpt: I track a commercial site's position on about a dozen money queries every Monday, two ways. A script calls a search API with the location set to the United States. And a browser agent, an AI that driv…
articles.body: I track a commercial site's position on about a dozen money queries every Monday, two ways. A script calls a search API with the location set to the United States. And a browser agent, an AI that drives a real browser, runs the same queries in a private, signed-out window and reports what Google shows: positions, the top three results, whether an AI Overview appears and who it cites. Two methods, so that one can catch the other's mistakes. This Monday they disagreed about everything. The script said my site had slipped from #1–2 to #4–6 on its main queries over two weeks, and a competitor now held #1 on all of them. The browser check said my site was #1 on three of those queries and was the first source cited in Google's AI Overview.

articles.title: Astronomers witness a star eating its companion in 1st-of-its-kind observation
articles.excerpt: Astronomers may have, for the first time ever, directly witnessed a star engulfing its stellar companion.
articles.body: Astronomers may have, for the first time ever, directly witnessed a star engulfing its companion, a new study reports. As stars die, they swell up to hundreds of times their original size, consuming anything orbiting nearby. In a binary star system, this can include a dying star merging with its companion star. However, scientists had never directly seen any examples of such a cosmic drama unfolding — until now. "Catching a star engulfing its companion in the act is very difficult," study lead author Viraj Karambelkar, an astrophysicist at Columbia University in New York, told Space.com. "When a star engulfs its companion, its effect is very subtle — like throwing a bucket of water in a large ocean.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 18, 2013: NASA launches MAVEN spacecraft to Mars to find out how the Red Planet lost its water
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 18, 2013, NASA launched the MAVEN spacecraft to Mars to investigate the planet's missing water. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 18, 2013, NASA launched the MAVEN spacecraft to Mars. The name of NASA's MAVEN spacecraft stands for Mars Atmosphere and Volatile EvolutioN. The spacecraft was an orbiter designed to help scientists figure out what happened to the water on Mars and its atmosphere. Mars is dry today, but it data from several Mars missions suggest that it was a much wetter environment a long time ago. MAVEN tracked the rate of atmospheric loss from Mars . The planet has a super thin atmosphere that has been leaking into space for a few billion years. Scientists think that when Mars lost its atmosphere, water dried up on the surface as a result. Solar storms that blast radiation into the solar system appear to have blasted away some of the atmosphere.
